ideas: Deep knowledge and trust built over years
Faster salary growth from changing jobs
Whether companies are loyal to staff anymore

phrases.meaning: know-how about how a company works

model: I think loyalty is still valuable, but it's not as rewarded as it used to be. On the positive side, people who stay put for many years build up a lot of institutional knowledge, and they earn their managers' trust, so they're often given important projects. My manager, for example, has been working at our company for twelve years, and she's worked her way up from an assistant to a director. On the other hand, a lot of young people now see job-hopping as the fastest way to climb the career ladder. Several of my friends have changed jobs three times since graduating, and each time they've got a bigger pay rise than they would have got by staying. Also, loyalty is a two-way street. Many companies have laid off long-serving staff during difficult times, so employees don't feel they owe them much. So overall, I'd say loyalty makes sense if the company is investing in you, but nobody should stay somewhere just out of habit.
